This matches this record's father, John McArthur (I182381537173, born/died at Milton, Dunoon, Argyll per the tree), by name and place. The 'Moir' surname persisting as a middle name in the 2002 Chief's own name (James Edward MOIR MacArthur) three centuries later strongly corroborates this Margaret's marriage to a Moir and her place in a real, continuing family line — this is very unlikely to be coincidence.

No source anywhere gives Margaret's own birth year; 1664, combined with the externally-confirmed ~1775 death, produces the impossible 111-year lifespan the audit tool flagged. The tree's own import data for this small family is already internally inconsistent on years (her father John McArthur's record separately carries THREE different unsourced birth-year guesses — 1650 in vitals, Abt.1640/1645/1640 across duplicate GEDCOM events — and two conflicting death-year guesses, 1694 and 1697, versus the external source's ~1674), consistent with a garbled/mistyped year rather than a real 111-year life. Given husband Alexander Moir's recorded birth (1679) and son James Moir's recorded death (1784), Margaret's true birth was most plausibly in the 1680s-1690s (age roughly 85-95 at death — long-lived but credible, unlike 111). No document fixes an exact year, so this is left an open question rather than a fabricated replacement date; see docs/research/ancestors/gen11-margaret-mcarthur.md.
